title: Article 228A — Special provisions as to disposal of questions relating to constitutional validity of State laws (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 228A imposed special procedural restrictions on High Court disposal of questions relating to the constitutional validity of State laws. It was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13 April 1978).
content.glance: Art 228A omitted by 43rd Amendment 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). Special HC disposition rules for State-law validity removed.
content.study:
Article 228A was part of the Emergency-era package restricting judicial handling of constitutionality questions.

Omission: Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978).

Living frame: High Courts dispose of constitutional questions under Articles 226, 227, 228 and applicable procedure; Article 228A is not living law.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 228A as a current procedural requirement.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Inserted by the 42nd Amendment; omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978).

misconceptions.trap: Article 228A still governs how High Courts dispose of State-law validity questions.
misconceptions.correction: Article 228A was omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977. It is not living law.
